items.stem: What is meant by “birth rate (natality)”?
items.answer: The number of births per capita in a population in a given period.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the number of births per capita in a population in a given period.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about population attributes is correct?
items.answer: Pug marks and faecal pellets can be used to estimate tiger populations.
items.markingKey: (d) Pug marks and faecal pellets can be used to estimate tiger populations. The other statements are false. Birth rate is an attribute of a population, not of an individual. Population density always has to be measured in numbers.
A triangular age pyramid indicates a declining population.

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
A forest department team in Madhya Pradesh wants to know the number of tigers in a reserve.
(i) Why is a direct count not practical? (1 mark)
(ii) Name two indirect methods used. (1 mark)
(iii) Why is relative density often enough for ecological studies? Give an example. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Tigers are elusive and range over large areas. (ii) Pug marks and faecal pellets (also camera traps). (iii) Absolute numbers are not always needed; relative density serves the purpose, e.g. the number of fish caught per trap is a good measure of the fish population in a lake.

items.stem: Which of the following is an attribute of an individual?
items.answer: birth
items.markingKey: (a) Birth is an attribute of an individual; the others are not.

age distribution
pug marks
number of fish caught per trap

items.stem: Draw and explain the three types of age pyramids of human populations.
items.answer: Expanding: triangular with a broad base of pre-reproductive individuals (growing). Stable: bell-shaped, pre-reproductive and reproductive groups about equal. Declining: urn-shaped with a narrow base (fewer young). The shape reflects the growth status of the population.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each diagram; ½ mark each interpretation.

immigration
a population

items.answer: Biomass or per cent cover is a better measure of population size when individuals differ greatly in size.

items.stem: In a grassland there were 20 rabbits last year. In one year 5 new ones are added through reproduction. Calculate the birth rate.
items.answer: 0.25 per individual per year

items.stem:
Students in Bengaluru grow yeast in a flask with a fixed amount of glucose and count cells daily.
(i) What shape of growth curve do they expect? (1 mark)
(ii) Name the growth model. (1 mark)
(iii) Why does growth eventually stop, and what is that population size called? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Sigmoid (S-shaped). (ii) Logistic (Verhulst–Pearl) growth. (iii) Glucose and space are limited; as resources are used up and wastes build up, birth rate falls to equal death rate; the maximum population supported is the carrying capacity (K).

items.stem: A population of 50 individuals grows exponentially with an intrinsic rate of natural increase r = 0.3 per year. Using Nₜ = N₀eʳᵗ, calculate the population after 2 years. (Take e = 2.718)
items.answer: ≈ 91 individuals

items.stem: If r for a population is 0.1 per year and K = 1000, when is the absolute growth rate the highest? Explain.
items.answer: dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K is a maximum when N = K/2 = 500 individuals, i.e. at the inflection point of the sigmoid curve, where dN/dt = 0.1 × 500 × 0.5 = 25 per year.
items.markingKey: 1 mark N = K/2; 1 mark calculation.

items.stem: A population follows logistic growth with r = 0.4 per year and carrying capacity K = 1000. Using dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K, find the growth rate when N = 900.

items.stem: Compare exponential and logistic growth with equations and graphs. Which is more realistic and why?
items.answer: Exponential: dN/dt = rN, Nₜ = N₀eʳᵗ; unlimited resources; J-shaped curve. Logistic (Verhulst–Pearl): dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K; limited resources; sigmoid curve with lag, acceleration, deceleration and asymptote at carrying capacity K. Logistic growth is more realistic because resources in nature are finite and competition increases as N approaches K.
items.markingKey: 2 marks exponential; 2 marks logistic; 1 mark realism.

items.stem:

items.answer: (i) Commensalism. (ii) It has lost its chlorophyll and leaves and derives nutrition from the host plant, harming it. (iii) Mutualism: the alga makes food by photosynthesis; the fungus provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals.

items.markingKey: (i) cactus – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: morphological defence – 1 mark. (iii) for Calotropis: cardiac glycosides; chemical defence; cattle and goats do not browse it – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: What is meant by “exponential growth”?
items.answer: J-shaped growth in which the population grows in geometric fashion when resources are unlimited.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: J-shaped growth in which the population grows in geometric fashion when resources are unlimited.

items.stem: Which sign combination (species A/species B) describes mutualism? (+ beneficial, − detrimental, 0 neutral)
items.markingKey: (b) Mutualism: +/+.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Population density always has to be measured in numbers.
Reason (R): Pug marks and faecal pellets can be used to estimate tiger populations.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Per cent cover or biomass can be more meaningful, e.g. a few large banyan trees vs many Parthenium plants. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: In a town survey, 20% of people are pre-reproductive, 42% reproductive and 38% post-reproductive. What would be the shape of its age pyramid and what does it show?
items.answer: urn-shaped (narrow base); the population is declining
items.markingKey: (b) A large pre-reproductive base ⇒ triangular (growing); nearly equal pre- and reproductive groups ⇒ bell-shaped (stable); a small base ⇒ urn-shaped (declining). Here: urn-shaped (narrow base); the population is declining.
options: triangular (broad base); the population is growing
urn-shaped (narrow base); the population is declining
bell-shaped; the population is stable
urn-shaped (narrow base); the population is growing

items.stem: Which of the following statements about population growth is incorrect?
items.answer: The carrying capacity is the minimum population a habitat supports.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “The carrying capacity is the minimum population a habitat supports.” Correct form: It is the maximum population the habitat can support.
options: The carrying capacity is the minimum population a habitat supports.
In nature resources are finite, so logistic growth is more realistic.
Exponential growth gives a J-shaped curve.
Logistic growth gives a sigmoid curve with lag, log, deceleration and asymptote phases.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about population growth is correct?
items.answer: The r value for the human population in India in 1981 was 0.0205.
items.markingKey: (b) The r value for the human population in India in 1981 was 0.0205. The other statements are false. It occurs only when resources are unlimited. It is the maximum population the habitat can support. r = b − d.
options: Exponential growth occurs when resources are limited.
The r value for the human population in India in 1981 was 0.0205.
r is the sum of per capita birth and death rates.
The carrying capacity is the minimum population a habitat supports.

items.stem: Which term describes the number of individuals of the same species that have come into the habitat from elsewhere during a given period?
items.answer: immigration
items.markingKey: (c) Immigration: the number of individuals of the same species that have come into the habitat from elsewhere during a given period.
options: an age pyramid
death rate (mortality)
immigration
birth rate (natality)

items.stem: A plant defends itself against herbivores by: desert plant; morphological defence; spines (modified leaves). Identify the plant. Give a reason.
items.answer: Cactus
items.markingKey: 1 mark: cactus; 1 mark: the features desert plant; morphological defence; spines (modified leaves) are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Parasites always kill their hosts quickly.
Reason (R): In lichens the fungus and alga live in mutualism.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Parasites usually harm but do not quickly kill hosts; they reduce survival, growth and reproduction. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which sign combination (species A/species B) describes competition? (+ beneficial, − detrimental, 0 neutral)
items.markingKey: (c) Competition: −/−.

items.stem: A population of 100 individuals grows exponentially with an intrinsic rate of natural increase r = 0.02 per year. Using Nₜ = N₀eʳᵗ, calculate the population after 2 years. (Take e = 2.718)
items.answer: ≈ 104 individuals

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT an attribute of an individual?
items.answer: faecal pellets
items.markingKey: (a) Faecal pellets is an indirect way to estimate population size, not an attribute of an individual.
options: faecal pellets
sex (male or female)
birth
death

items.stem: Explain the term “resource partitioning”.
items.answer: A mechanism of co-existence in which competing species choose different times or patterns for feeding, as in MacArthur's warblers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a mechanism of co-existence in which competing species choose different times or patterns for feeding, as in MacArthur's warblers.

items.stem: In a town survey, 35% of people are pre-reproductive, 33% reproductive and 32% post-reproductive. What would be the shape of its age pyramid and what does it show?
items.answer: bell-shaped; the population is stable
items.markingKey: (c) A large pre-reproductive base ⇒ triangular (growing); nearly equal pre- and reproductive groups ⇒ bell-shaped (stable); a small base ⇒ urn-shaped (declining). Here: bell-shaped; the population is stable.
options: urn-shaped (narrow base); the population is declining
bell-shaped; the population is declining
bell-shaped; the population is stable

items.stem: Which of the following statements about population attributes is correct?
items.answer: A population has attributes that an individual organism does not.
items.markingKey: (d) A population has attributes that an individual organism does not. The other statements are false. Birth rate is an attribute of a population, not of an individual. A triangular pyramid with a broad base indicates an expanding population. Per cent cover or biomass can be more meaningful, e.g. a few large banyan trees vs many Parthenium plants.
options: Population density always has to be measured in numbers.
An individual organism has a birth rate.
A triangular age pyramid indicates a declining population.
A population has attributes that an individual organism does not.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A population growing exponentially gives a J-shaped curve.
Reason (R): Under unlimited resources the per capita growth rate stays constant.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) dN/dt = rN.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

items.stem: A population follows logistic growth with r = 0.5 per year and carrying capacity K = 1000. Using dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K, find the growth rate when N = 750.
items.answer: 93.8 individuals per year
